problem_title: How large must the maximum degree of a triangle-free graph of diameter at most two be?
original_question_en: How large must the maximum degree of a triangle-free graph of diameter at most two be?  (Erdos-Pach Problem 1.3: with f(n) the least maximum degree of a triangle-free graph of diameter at most two on n vertices, what is the order of growth of f(n)?  Catalog status: Solved.)
statement_of_jsp_000139_main: Let G be a triangle-free graph of diameter at most two on a finite vertex set of size n, with all degrees at most d.  Then n <= d*d + 1 (Moore bound), equivalently Delta^2 >= n - 1 over the reals.  This is the 'how large must the maximum degree be' half of JSP-000139; the complementary construction side (f(n) = Theta(sqrt n), Hanson-Seyffarth 1984 / Furedi-Seress 1994 / Haviv-Levy 2018) is not formalised.
